The test image shows a corn ear with husks peeled back, revealing orange/yellow kernels and a large dark brown/black dusty/sooty mass at the base/tip of the ear. This strongly suggests smut disease.

Let me check reference images starting with Common_Smut and Head_Smut as top candidates.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image**: Two corn ears with husks peeled back. The lower ear has a large dark brown/dusty crumbly mass occupying the base, while the rest of both ears show normal orange/yellow kernels.

**Reference comparison summary**:
- Common Smut (176, 218): Large white/gray-to-black galls on ears — structurally similar, the brown/dusty mass in test could be a mature/dried smut gall
- Head Smut: Affects the tassel/head, not ear base — does not match
- Diplodia Ear Rot: White mold at ear base — does not match color
- Gibberella: Pink/white mold on kernels — does not match
- Fusarium: White/pink patches on kernels — does not match
- Aspergillus: Green powdery mold — does not match
- Trichoderma: Blue-green mold over kernels — does not match
- Leaf diseases (Gray Leaf Spot, Northern Leaf Blight, Southern Rust, Eyespot, Tar Spot): All affect leaves, not ears

The large fungal mass replacing the lower portion of an ear while normal kernels remain above is most characteristic of **Common Smut** (Ustilago maydis). The brownish/dusty appearance is consistent with mature, dried smut galls where the outer membrane has broken down and teliospores are exposed.
